description.from:
## Problem
Draft MDX (`state: draft`) is hard to review on production. That friction pushes premature `state: published` so reviewers can see the item on live `/posts/` and `/blog/` lists.

## Goal
Add a special, intentional preview mode (URL query param or equivalent) that, when present, shows **draft + published** items on the posts list and the blog list — i.e. what those index pages would look like if every current draft were published. Default (no flag) stays published-only for public visitors.

## Scope
- `/posts/` (and paginated posts pages if any)
- `/blog/` (and related collection list pages if they also filter `state: published`)
- Not a requirement to change individual permalinks unless needed for review; focus is the index/list views so drafts are findable in production.

## Constraints / notes
- Must not leak drafts into the normal public list. Flag should be explicit and easy for the team, not accidental SEO.
- Prefer something that works on production without a local build (that is the point).
- Implementation detail open: query param (e.g. `?drafts=1`), cookie, or path — pick the simplest safe option.
- Gatsby static generation may require baking draft rows into page-data and gating client-side, or a separate preview page/route — call that out in the design before shipping.

## Success
Team can leave articles in `draft`, open production with the preview flag, see drafts in the lists, and review without publishing early.
description.to:
## Problem
Draft MDX (`state: draft`) is hard to review on production. That friction pushes premature `state: published` so reviewers can see the item on live `/posts/` and `/blog/` lists. Content is authored across many agents and IDEs, so preview must work from the live site itself — not from any one coding tool or machine.

## Goal
Add a special, intentional production preview mode that, when unlocked, shows **draft + published** items on the posts list and the blog list — i.e. what those index pages would look like if every current draft were published. Default (locked) stays published-only for public visitors and crawlers.

## Hard requirements (Ryan 2026-09-09)
- **Secret password required** to unlock draft visibility. Do not expose every draft to the open web or to arbitrary scrapers/AIs.
- **Server-side enforcement** (or trusted edge): do not ship draft payloads to anonymous browsers and merely hide them client-side.
- **Site-centric:** unlock works on production without a local build.

## Scope
- `/posts/` (and paginated posts pages if any)
- `/blog/` (and related collection list pages if they also filter `state: published`)
- Individual permalinks only as needed for review after unlock; avoid accidental SEO of drafts.

## Constraints / notes
- Implementation detail open: query param carrying/proving the secret, cookie after password form, or path — pick the simplest safe option that stays server-enforced.
- Gatsby static generation may require baking draft rows into page-data with a server/edge gate, a separate preview route, or SSR/ISR — call that out in the design before shipping.
- Papyrus-platform mirror (multi-site): initiative `PPY-c40638` on AnthusAI/Papyrus for Pilobol.us, P.apyr.us, threat-intelligence.anth.us, etc.

## Success
Team can leave articles in `draft`, open production with the secret unlock, see drafts in the lists, and review without publishing early — without leaking drafts publicly.
